title: A whole-mount immunohistochemistry protocol for detection of mouse corneal nerves
protocol: Dissect the corneas using surgical spring scissors and forceps under a binocular dissecting microscope.
Hold the posterior part of the eye softly with forceps.
Make the first incision upon the sclera with the tip of the surgical spring scissors.
Enlarge the incision and make it a circular cut to eliminate part of the sclera that is attached to the optic nerve.
Gently press the eye ball to push out the lens.
Make radial incisions to the central cornea and gently scrape off the retina with the tip of the scissors.
Gently scrape off the iris with the tip of the scissors.
Cut off the sclera, making sure to allow for a generous margin at the limbus to include nerves at the corneal/limbal interface.
Dissect a mouse eye immersed in 1× PBS under a microscope using scissor and forceps.
Wash one cornea per well in a 96-well plate with 1× PBS five times for five minutes each at 20°C–25°C.
Pipette off 1× PBS after the final wash.
Add permeabilization buffer (1% Triton-X100 in 1× PBS) to the wells containing the corneas.
Incubate on a low-speed orbital shaker at 20°C–25°C for 60 minutes.
Transfer the corneas using fine-tip forceps into new wells.
Add 20% serum in blocking buffer (0.3% Triton-X100/0.1% Tween-20 in 1× PBS) to the new wells.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 minutes.
Transfer corneas into new wells.
Add a 100 μL cocktail of primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer to each well.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 2 h, followed by an additional incubation for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Wash the corneas in washing buffer (0.1% Tween-20 in 1× PBS) five times/5 minutes.
Transfer the corneas into new wells (or new tubes).
Add a 100 μL cocktail of secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer (1:500 dilution) to each well.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 2 hours.
Wash the corneas with washing buffer five times/10 minutes.
Mount the corneas on slides with the epithelium apposed to the #1.5 coverslip (170 μm).
Place only one cornea per slide.
Dry the slides at 4°C for at least 12 hours before imaging.
Turn on the upright Olympus IX81 Fluoview 1000 laser scanning confocal microscope equipped with a 20× oil (numerical aperture 0.85) objective lens and an automated stage.
Set up the system to do ZDC stitched mosaics with 10% overlap of the images for good registration.
Define the boundary of the cornea in the mosaic outline, allowing generous margins around the cornea.
Focus the objective and set up the start and stop points of the z-scan spanning from the epithelium to the endothelium.
Check the z settings at multiple locations in the tissue to ensure that the entire cornea will be included in the stacks.
Go to File and Folder, save the scanning files.
Check “Auto create sub folder every experiment.”
Check “Set Track info to FV with position movement.”
Re-Register to include all the points selected in step 19.
Check Ready button and then start scanning.
Save images in the native Olympus Image Binary (OIB) format or an OIF format.
Go to MATL Viewer under Devices.
Click Open MATL-Log File.
Choose the MATL Mosaic file from the data folder.
Press the Select Action button.
Select the areas that need to be stitched and click Stitch.
Check all channels that need to be stitched.
Check Correction and Smoothing.
Press the Show button.
After stitching, save the file with the original name in the native OIB format.
Make sure to check Apply to Series.
